categories.name: AI & ML Security
categories.summary: This category highlights the intersection of AI/ML and security, covering both offensive and defensive applications. Key themes include LLM-driven vulnerability research automation, securing local AI agents on endpoints, and the emergence of malvertising campaigns targeting AI tools. Microsoft's approach to endpoint security for local AI agents represents a significant enterprise security development.

key_items.title: LLM-Driven Vulnerability Research Automation
key_items.detail: Claroty's Team82 explores hands-free vulnerability research leveraging large language models, demonstrating how AI can automate security analysis workflows.

key_items.title: Microsoft Defender Secures Local AI Agents
key_items.detail: Microsoft announces endpoint security capabilities specifically designed to protect local AI agents, marking a new frontier in AI-aware endpoint protection.

key_items.title: LLMShare Malvertising Campaign Discovered
key_items.detail: Push Security uncovers a malvertising campaign dubbed 'LLMShare' that exploits interest in AI/LLM tools to distribute malicious payloads.

categories.name: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities & CVEs
categories.summary: Vulnerability research tools and methodologies are advancing, with Berkeley launching a vulnerability database resource. Additionally, research demonstrates testing AI models against FreeBSD systems for local exploitation scenarios, showcasing the growing role of open-weight models in security research.

key_items.title: Berkeley Vulnerability Research Portal
key_items.detail: UC Berkeley launches vuln.cs.berkeley.edu, providing a centralized resource for vulnerability research and security analysis.

key_items.title: FreeBSD Local Exploitation with Open-Weight Models
key_items.detail: Research explores using open-weight AI models for FreeBSD local vulnerability testing, demonstrating system-over-model security testing approaches.

categories.name: Industry News & Policy
categories.summary: A significant corporate accountability story emerged with whistleblower allegations against IBM regarding concealed data breaches. This raises broader questions about enterprise transparency and breach disclosure practices in the tech industry.

key_items.title: IBM Whistleblower Alleges Data Breach Cover-ups
key_items.detail: A former cyber executive turned whistleblower accuses IBM of systematically covering up multiple data breaches, potentially exposing major compliance and transparency failures.

key_items.title: AI Security Newsletter - May 2026
key_items.detail: Monthly digest covering AI security research, insights, reports, events, tools, and resources curated for the AI security community.

top_insights: LLM-powered security tooling is maturing rapidly, with both offensive (vulnerability research automation) and defensive (endpoint AI agent protection) applications emerging simultaneously.
Malvertising campaigns are now specifically targeting AI/LLM tool users, indicating threat actors recognize this growing attack surface.
Enterprise AI security is becoming a distinct product category, as evidenced by Microsoft's dedicated Defender capabilities for local AI agents.
Corporate accountability in cybersecurity remains a challenge, with whistleblower allegations against major tech companies highlighting gaps in breach disclosure practices.
Academic institutions like Berkeley are contributing essential vulnerability research infrastructure to the security community.
